question_text: In an attempt to create other selective dopamine 1 (D1) agonists, a small pharmaceutical company created a cell-based chemical screen that involved three modified receptors - alpha 1 (A1), beta 1 (B1), and D1. In the presence of D1 stimulation, the cell would produce an mRNA that codes for a fluorescent protein; however, if the A1 or B1 receptors are also stimulated at the same time, the cells would degrade the mRNA of the fluorescent protein thereby preventing it from being produced. Which of the following would best serve as a positive control for this experiment?

                    ### Question
                    In an attempt to create other selective dopamine 1 (D1) agonists, a small pharmaceutical company created a cell-based chemical screen that involved three modified receptors - alpha 1 (A1), beta 1 (B1), and D1. In the presence of D1 stimulation, the cell would produce an mRNA that codes for a fluorescent protein; however, if the A1 or B1 receptors are also stimulated at the same time, the cells would degrade the mRNA of the fluorescent protein thereby preventing it from being produced. Which of the following would best serve as a positive control for this experiment?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Bromocriptine
opb. Dobutamine
opc. Dopamine
opd. Epinephrine
ope. Fenoldopam

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Dopamine and Fenoldopam both stimulate the D1 receptor, leading to the production of mRNA for the fluorescent protein, making them suitable positive controls for the experiment. The evidence path confirming the interaction of Dopamine with the Dopamine D1 receptor supports their role as positive controls.
